data.summary: The pod startup for eval-svc-75fdff78d5-jkxm7 took 31.0 seconds, significantly exceeding the 10.0-second SLO. This delay was primarily caused by the model.download phase, which consumed 25.006 seconds. The model weights were downloaded from a remote store on every start, as indicated by a cache miss.

findings.statement: The pod startup took 31.0 seconds, exceeding the SLO of 10.0 seconds.
The `model.download` phase was the longest contributor to the startup time, taking 25.006 seconds.
The `model.download` operation reported `cache_hit: false`, indicating the model weights were downloaded from a remote store on every start.
The `app_init` phase, which encompasses model loading, lasted 26.09 seconds.

ruled_out.reason: The `scheduling` phase duration was 0.0 seconds, and there were 0 `failed_scheduling_events`, indicating no capacity issues prevented scheduling.
The `image_pull` duration was 4.269 seconds for an image of 53328919 bytes, which is not the primary cause of the 31.0-second startup.
The `image_pull` throughput was 12492134 bytes/s, which is a normal rate and not indicative of a slow registry.
The `readiness` phase duration was 0.0 seconds, and there were 0 `probe_failures_after_app_ready`, indicating the readiness probe was not a bottleneck.

recommendations.rationale: To prevent repeated downloads, keep model weights on a persistent volume, pre-populated by a prefetch job, and enable the application's cache reuse. This will allow subsequent starts to load from local disk.
